doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Flying with the alto; soprano and tenor
summary: Travels light with alto; has tried soprano and tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Has traveling gotten somewhat better for you?
I mean you have to fly to most of your gigs, don’t you?
Oh yeah. I usually fly out of Syracuse and get a connecting flight out of Syracuse usually and go out to California and New Orleans.
You are able to take your horn on the plane?
Um hum. I travel light too. Like it’s just this and a duffle bag usually, and like a backpack. Or you know some of the guys have big huge suitcases, and it just takes up too much space.
Yeah. Well it’s a good thing you stuck with the alto.
Rather than a horn that you’d have an issue with. Did you ever mess with the soprano or be tempted to?

I did, a little bit. And tenor too. I just really want to get a tenor soon. But I did like both and you know what’s funny? Whenever I pick up a tenor I immediately want to play jazz. I start playing [scats] but when I’m on the alto I’m like [scats] so it’s like two different instruments actually.
